title: When temporary works outlive the programme, the brief needs revisiting
excerpt: HSE’s temporary works FAQs note the tendency to assume short-lived temporary works are less important. That is incorrect. An October 2026 industry insight highlights that when the programme moves, the load is still checked but the period of use is not always revisited. Longer temporary states meet more weather, nearby activity and opportunities for unconsidered loading. Coordination under HSE guidance and BS 5975-1:2024 covers the whole life of the temporary works, not only design.
linkedinReady:
When the programme slips, the temporary works brief does not automatically update itself.

HSE’s temporary works FAQs make the point plainly. Temporary works may be in place for only a short while, and there is a tendency to assume they are less important. That is incorrect. Lack of care with design, selection and assembly leaves temporary works liable to fail or collapse. The same guidance notes that temporary works can be sensitive to how they are used and are easily affected by other work taking place nearby. Failures are often linked to loadings that were underestimated.

An October 2026 industry insight from EE&HL Network draws out the practical consequence: when the programme moves, the load is still checked; the period of use is not always revisited. A longer temporary state can meet more weather, more nearby activity, more changes of crew, and more opportunities for an adjacent trade to lean on it, remove a brace or load it in a way that was not considered. None of this requires a single dramatic event.

HSE describes temporary works coordination as including making sure temporary works are correctly installed, used, checked and maintained — across their whole life, not only at design. BS 5975-1:2024 sets out the Temporary Works Coordinator role as industry good practice. A change in programme that extends the temporary state is a change worth sending back to the designer and checker under the project procedure.

Identify the expected period of use in the design brief. When that period is exceeded, treat it as a review trigger. Confirm that the original assumptions (loads, weather, adjacent activity, inspection regime) still hold before the temporary works continue to be relied upon.

Provisional category only — to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure. Do not proceed until reviewed and accepted under the project temporary works procedure.

Educational only. Not for construction.

body.p: HSE’s Temporary works FAQs state that the same degree of care and attention must be given to the design and construction of temporary works as to the permanent works. Because temporary works may be in place for only a short while, there is a tendency to assume they are less important. This is incorrect. Lack of care with design, selection, assembly and so on leaves temporary works liable to fail or collapse, placing people at risk of injury and causing project delay. The same guidance notes that temporary works can be very sensitive to how they are used and are easily affected by other work taking place nearby, and that failure is often found to result from the loadings being underestimated. HSE describes coordinating temporary works as including planning where and when they will be needed and ensuring they are correctly installed, used, checked and maintained. On 9 October 2026 EE&HL Network published an insight titled “When Temporary Works Stay in Place Too Long”. It observes that temporary works design and management depend on the loads, the conditions and the anticipated period of use. When the programme moves, the load is still checked; the period of use is not always revisited. A longer temporary state can meet more weather, more nearby activity, more changes of crew and more opportunities for an adjacent trade to lean on it, remove a brace or load it in a way nobody considered. The insight lists typical causes (weather windows slipping, plant or crew not ready, another scope finishing first, open decisions deferred to site) and notes that the UK framework already provides for coordination across the whole life of the temporary works. BS 5975-1:2024 sets out management procedures and the Temporary Works Coordinator role as industry good practice; HSE notes there is no legal requirement to use that job title, but that the Standard provides a consensus view of good practice.

Temporary works are an engineered solution used to support or protect a structure during construction, support plant or equipment, retain the sides of an excavation, or provide access. CDM 2015 requires the principal contractor to plan, manage and monitor the construction phase and requires contractors to plan, manage and monitor their own work. BS 5975-1:2024 sets out a temporary works procedure as industry good practice; it is not a statute. Exact clause references should be confirmed against the project’s licensed copy. The period of use is an assumption that belongs in the design brief. When that period is exceeded because the programme has moved, the temporary works may be meeting conditions that were not the basis of the original design, check or inspection regime. Standard does not automatically mean low risk when the temporary state has outlived its brief. A prop, brace, falsework tower or excavation support that was adequate for a planned few weeks can become higher consequence if it remains in place through additional weather events, adjacent trade activity or unconsidered loading. Provisional category only — to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: State the expected period of use, the design loads, the weather and adjacent-activity assumptions, and the inspection and maintenance regime in the design brief before the temporary works are designed.
Treat any extension of the planned period of use as a change that requires review under the project temporary works procedure before the temporary works continue to be relied upon.
Send the extended period, the revised adjacent activities and any changed loading or weather exposure back to the temporary works designer and checker.
Confirm that the original assumptions still hold, or that a revised design/check has been accepted, before loading or continued use is permitted.
Include the whole life of the temporary works (installation, use, checking, maintenance and removal) in the coordination role. Do not treat design acceptance as the end of control.
After adverse weather, nearby activity, crew changes or any event that could affect stability, inspect and, where necessary, stop and review before work continues.
At the point of removal or striking, confirm that the permanent structure is ready to take the load and that the removal sequence itself has been reviewed.
Do not proceed until the arrangement, including any extended period, has been reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.

body.p: Educational briefing only. Not for construction. Based on HSE Temporary works FAQs and the EE&HL Network insight of 9 October 2026. It is not a design, a check or a statement that any particular temporary works arrangement is adequate or inadequate. No loads, residual capacities or revised designs have been calculated here. Subject to project-specific verification and acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. AI-assisted drafting requires competent review before use on site.
